::: {.project-intro}
**Research question.** How do differences in economic output, inflation and international trade contribute to measured economic distance between the United States and other countries in 2019?
:::

This project revisits an earlier empirical assignment using **R and Quarto** to improve transparency and reproducibility. The original project was coauthored by Chipo Jaya and Xianghan Zhu; this Quarto adaptation is a new analytical presentation of the study.

::: {.callout-important}
## Measurement correction
The original report described the income variable as *GDP per capita*, but the uploaded workbook contains **GDP (constant 2015 US$), i.e., total GDP** (`NY.GDP.MKTP.KD`). This reproducible version uses the workbook's actual measure and does **not** label it GDP per capita. A follow-up sensitivity analysis should replace total GDP with GDP per capita and compare rankings.
:::

## Dataset overview

```{r}
#| label: data-overview
cat('The uploaded workbook contains', nrow(raw), 'data rows. After excluding aggregate entries and incomplete country observations,', nrow(data), 'countries remain.\n')
cat('The reference country (USA) is included among these observations; the distance ranking excludes it.\n')
```

The four indicators are total real GDP (constant 2015 US$), imports of goods and services (% of GDP), GDP-deflator inflation (annual %), and exports of goods and services (% of GDP). All refer to **2019**. See [Data & methodology](methods.qmd).

## Economic distance relative to the United States

For a four-indicator country vector $x_i$, US vector $x_{US}$ and sample covariance matrix $S$:

$$D(i,US)=\sqrt{(x_i-x_{US})^{\mathsf{T}}S^{-1}(x_i-x_{US})}.$$

This distance adjusts for both units and correlation among the indicators. **A larger distance indicates dissimilarity across these measured economic variables, not a judgment of a country's development, investment attractiveness or institutional quality.**

```{r}
#| label: tbl-distance-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Distance summary across non-US countries"
knitr::kable(distance_summary, digits=3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-closest
#| tbl-cap: "Ten smallest distances from the United States (excluding USA)"
knitr::kable(closest, digits=3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-farthest
#| tbl-cap: "Ten largest distances from the United States"
knitr::kable(farthest, digits=3)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ranked
#| fig-cap: "Countries at the nearest and farthest ends of the measured distance distribution"
#| fig-height: 7
plot_data <- bind_rows(closest |> mutate(group='Nearest'),
                       farthest |> mutate(group='Farthest')) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(country, ' (', group, ')'))
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=reorder(label, distance_us), y=distance_us, fill=group)) +
  geom_col(show.legend=FALSE) + coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales='free_y', ncol=1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c(Farthest='#7553a9',Nearest='#197654')) +
  labs(x=NULL,y='Mahalanobis distance to the USA') + theme_minimal(base_size=12)
```

## SDG relevance and interpretation

This cross-country comparison offers **context for SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals)**, especially international trade differences. **It does not directly calculate SDG Target 17.11**, which concerns the share of global exports originating in developing and least developed countries. Exports *as a share of a country's GDP* are a different measure. A subsequent ISS phase can incorporate the official 17.11 indicator to assess that target.

## Limitations and next steps

- Results depend on **one year (2019)** and on which countries have complete data.
- Total GDP captures economic scale and should not be interpreted as per-capita prosperity.
- The four indicators measure economic differences, **not** political, legal or cultural distance.
- Rankings are relative to this sample and the covariance matrix computed from it; sensitivity analyses should assess robustness to alternate GDP definitions and outliers.
- The next phase should examine the official SDG 17.11 indicator and compare results over time.

**Sources:** [World Bank World Development Indicators](https://databank.worldbank.org/source/world-development-indicators); Berry, Guillén & Zhou (2010), *An institutional approach to cross-national distance*, *Journal of International Business Studies*, 41, 1460–1480.
